_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Chapters 1-4 had none. Reach for one precise image or a plain statement instead. Ch. 10 and ch. 11 both rested it cleanly at zero — ch. 11 in particular kept catching near-misses in draft ('the way she does every morning', 'the way you look at a sum') and rewrote around every one of them. Due to come off rest at ch. 12; reintroduce sparingly, not as a reflex.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Name the actual object or action. Clean at zero in ch. 10 and ch. 11 (one near-miss in ch. 11 draft, 'cost a thing properly', caught and rewritten to 'price a job properly').

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: Lloyd's self-knowledge should show up as behaviour, not as narrated wisdom. A near-miss in ch. 10 ('I've learned to read the quiet...') was caught in revision and rewritten as direct observation — watch for this shape resurfacing.

Chapters 1-5 sit at roughly 6-12 per chapter. Keep long sentences where the rumination earns them; break them with short ones. Ch. 10 kept the count high but interleaved with a genuinely short-sentence argument scene (dialogue under 10 words a line) — lean harder on that contrast rather than reducing long-sentence count alone. Ch. 11 repeated that contrast with the Edie/relieving-officer exchange (clipped procedural dialogue against Lloyd's longer ruminative paragraphs) — this pairing is becoming a reliable, developed habit rather than a repeated tic.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: Used twice in ch. 10 while the-way-simile was resting; trimmed from an initial four. Clean at zero in ch. 11 — good sign it isn't hardening into the next tic, but keep watching since both rested constructions come off cooldown at ch. 12.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Appeared five times in ch. 10. Deliberately avoided in ch. 11 even though the chapter's subject (permits, ledgers, procedure) made it tempting — the literal paperwork was given to Edie's external ledger instead, and Lloyd's own interiority was kept physical/bodily rather than clerical. Treat as successfully evolved away from rather than due for reuse; if it returns, make it a new shape, not a repeat of ch. 10's phrasing.

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: New this chapter. Fits the project's flat, deflecting narration (Lloyd circling a thing he won't state plainly) but appeared three times in one chapter. Fine as a one-chapter cluster — watch for it recurring unchanged next chapter, which would mean it needs developing into a new shape rather than repeating.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: End on an action, an object or a line of dialogue.
